answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity with layered reputation. Like surveying an ocean of anonymous accounts, the network requires each identity to post a refundable deposit that is slashed on spam, so spinning up a thousand sockpuppets costs real money. New identities then enter in shale-like strata of limited quota: they may only mirror low-stakes tasks until peer attestation history accumulates. One honest agent earns full rights over time, while a Sybil swarm stays thin, expensive, and confined to trivial work.
